blocks.content: The President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court.

items: Article 222 requires consultation with the CJI and a 4-member SC Collegium before transferring High Court judges.
Transfers cannot be made as a punitive measure; they are valid only when executed in the public interest.
A judge transferred under Article 222 is entitled to a compensatory allowance determined by Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Under Article 222, the President can transfer a High Court judge to another High Court after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
The recommendation requires CJI consultation with a collegium of four senior-most Supreme Court judges.
Consultation must also include the Chief Justices of both the transferring and receiving High Courts.
Transferred judges receive a special compensatory allowance in addition to their salary as determined by Parliament.
Transfers are subject to judicial review and can only be executed in the public interest, not as a punitive measure.
